nodes.label: Minima Core Full Node Application
nodes.rationale: Deliberately excludes MDS and Maxima subsystems to keep a clean, minimal Minima-only node implementation.

nodes.label: Peer Bootstrap (peers action:addpeers)
nodes.rationale: No peers are hard-coded by default; users must supply a peer or peer-list URL, keeping bootstrap decentralized.

nodes.label: Solo Private Network Mode (-solo)
nodes.rationale: Recommended way to test Minima: run an isolated private chain, optionally wiped with -clean.

nodes.label: MegaMMR Node Mode (-megammr)
nodes.rationale: Stores all MMR data (exchange-style node) so other nodes can resync from it and sendfrom any account, versus the default single-user node.

nodes.label: PROOF Merkle Proof Function
nodes.rationale: Checks data, MMR proof, and root match — stated to be the same operation as mmrproof on Minima.

nodes.label: State Functions (STATE, PREVSTATE, SAMESTATE)
nodes.rationale: Per-transaction state variables enable stateful contracts across a sequence of UTXO transactions.

nodes.label: Generic FUNCTION Macro
nodes.rationale: Runs a script string after substituting $1..$n parameters, using returnvalue as result — KISS VM's reusable-subroutine mechanism.

nodes.label: SPHINCS Signature Verification KISS VM Script
nodes.rationale: On-chain SPHINCS verification in pure KISS VM. Inputs capped at 8 and outputs at 5 because the script would exceed the KISS VM 1024-operation limit; GETINID gives an unforgeable 32-byte per-coin hash so the signed message cannot be manipulated; each key position seeds the FORS tree so a key only ever signs one hash.
nodes.norm_label: sphincs signature verification kiss vm script

nodes.label: Transaction Message Hashing (incoins/outcoins SHA3)
nodes.rationale: Concatenates all input CoinIDs and every element of every output, then SHA3-hashes with @TOTIN/@TOTOUT so the signed message is unalterable for a given transaction — no forgery possible.

nodes.label: FORS Root Signature Check (Step 1)
nodes.rationale: CHECKSIG of the FORS root (STATE(101)) against the WOTS/SPHINCS public key; the same key always signs the same single hash, preserving one-time-signature safety.

nodes.label: HORST Tree Proof Verification Loop (Step 2)
nodes.rationale: 16 iterations, each PROOF-checking a HORST root against the FORS root and then the revealed pubkey against the HORST root at the message-derived index.

nodes.label: Minima Protocol
nodes.author: Spartacus Rex
nodes.rationale: Design goal is total decentralization above all: no miners, no rulers, no ever-growing database — small enough that every user runs a Complete node on a mobile phone forever, because centralized networks are easy to attack (fewer than 100 coerced humans could disrupt most coins).

nodes.label: Tx-PoW
nodes.author: Spartacus Rex
nodes.rationale: Removes paid miners by having every user PoW-mine their own transaction (~10s work); PoW pieces sum P2Pool-style into full blocks, so users both send transactions and construct the chain. Requires critical transaction mass — security is derived from transaction volume.

nodes.label: Maxima P2P Information Network
nodes.author: Spartacus Rex
nodes.rationale: Makes layer 2 secure layer 1 instead of replacing fee-based security: all Maxima messages pay PoW and all PoW secures Minima. Minima = value transfer (on-chain, flood-fill, does not scale); Maxima = information transfer (off-chain, point-to-point, scales).

nodes.label: Pulse Network
nodes.author: Spartacus Rex
nodes.rationale: PoW-backed PING: every node sends a valid Tx-PoW message (blank transaction, 10s work) every 10 minutes or is kicked off — pre-computed work usable for time-critical sends, peer mempool sync, and added chain security. No zombies allowed.

nodes.label: Distributed PoW
nodes.author: Spartacus Rex
nodes.rationale: Hash-rate does not equal security; its distribution does. With no mining rewards there is no incentive to acquire hash power, so no cartel approaches even 1% — a 51% attack has hardware cost but no recoupable reward. Caveat: requires a lot of users.

nodes.label: The Burn
nodes.author: Spartacus Rex
nodes.rationale: Replaces fees for DDoS defence: outputs summing below inputs 'pays' every holder via increased scarcity. No minimum needed since it funds no mining industry — it self-regulates as congestion control, transaction ordering, and spam prevention.

nodes.label: HashCash
nodes.author: Adam Back
nodes.rationale: First weaponized PoW (anti-spam DoS counter-measure); fully decentralized — each user mines and verifies independently. Minima Consensus is driven by HashCash and Burn, with users mining transactions instead of emails.

nodes.label: Cascading Proof Chain
nodes.author: Spartacus Rex
nodes.rationale: 256 Super Block levels (each twice the difficulty of the level below) let the proof chain grow logarithmically: almost limitless cumulative PoW stored in a finite header chain, so nearly all blocks/transactions are pruned with no security loss and a weekly-connecting user can still fully validate.

nodes.label: Storage-less MMR UTXO Database
nodes.author: Spartacus Rex
nodes.rationale: No global UTXO database: each user keeps only their own coins plus Merkle proofs against the MMR root ('your page of the book'), updated per block. Trade-off: users must stay up to date or need an archive node/friend to rediscover proofs (coin-proofs pose no security issue).

nodes.label: Minima Scripting Language (Smart Contracts, Tokens)
nodes.author: Spartacus Rex
nodes.rationale: Minima is a validatory network, not a computational one: validation is the minimum useful computation, logic is computed off-chain and validated on-chain. Scripts return TRUE/FALSE for spendability; state variables allow stateful contracts on a UTXO model; tokens are coloured Minima with zero extra cost. Key functions: MAST, VERIFYOUTPUT, VERIFYINPUT, ADDRESS, CHECKSIG, PROOF.

nodes.label: Quantum Secure Cryptography (KECCAK + WOTS)
nodes.author: Spartacus Rex
nodes.rationale: All security comes from hash functions (KECCAK; SHA2-256 for cross-chain hash locks) and Winternitz One-Time Signatures in Merkle trees, chosen so the protocol never needs a hard fork. Cost: signatures 10-20x larger than ECDSA (400-800 bytes), acceptable since almost all data is pruned.

nodes.label: Adaptive Block Size
nodes.author: Spartacus Rex
nodes.rationale: Max block size = 2x average of last n blocks, so users themselves steer it. User-centric chains need no full blocks or fee market — security is total PoW, and the Burn handles congestion.

nodes.label: GHOST Consensus
nodes.rationale: Tx-PoW suits GHOST because stale blocks are included as transactions in the main chain, letting the block tree be computed independently; enables the targeted 50-second block time.

nodes.label: Complete Node
nodes.author: Spartacus Rex
nodes.rationale: A node that both constructs and validates the chain. On Minima everyone runs one, so there are no user classes, no light-client attacks, and no soft forks — only hard forks, which are never required.

nodes.label: Immutable / Ossified Protocol
nodes.author: Spartacus Rex
nodes.rationale: Complete-from-inception with all scaling built in: a decentralized protocol can only grow in adoption once it stops being updated (cf. POP3, SMTP, UDP, TCP/IP). No soft forks allowed, no hard forks required.
